JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to General Hospital, Kanakapura and after first aid she was shifted to CDSIMER Hospital, Harohalli, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and underwent several examinations and was discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest and regular followup treatment.
She spent huge amount towards her treatment.
Further at the time of accident she was hale and healthy and was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m, by doing silkworm moth, caterpiller work at Kanakapura Town.
Due to the accidental injuries she became disabled and lost her earning capacity.

As the accident was caused by the reckless driving of the drivers of Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF- 8055 and KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent No.2 did not appear despite due service of notice of the petition upon him.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.1/KSRTC Transport Corporation contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
It is alleged that the petition is bad for mis-joinder of un-necessary parties.
It is contended that the driver of the KSRTC bus was no way responsible for the accident.
This respondent denied the rash and negligent act of the driver of its bus driver.
On the contrary it is stated that on the date and time of alleged accident the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Kanakapura to Halaguru.
The driver of the KSRTC Bhagyalakshmi S vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196267738/
2 bus drive the same in slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while so proceeding on Kanakapura - Halaguru Main road, near Kemmale Gate at that point of time Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 came from the opposite side, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with terrific speed in a zig-zag manner, observing the same the bus driver sensing some mishap, slowed down the speed of the bus and taken to its left side and when the things stood thus, car just like a bolt from the blue,
came to its extreme right side of the road, by crossing the midpoint, the driver of the bus, that too to extreme his right edge of the road, to avoid being hit by the car swear the bus to the little bit right side, but inspite of the same the driver of the car, due to the over speed and as the car moving in a zig zag manner totally lost control over the car and dashed violently against the bus and caused the accident, and due to the terrific hit by the car the bus moved to the right side.
As such, for the alleged accident the driver of the Qualis car was wholly and solely responsible, but the driver of bus in question was no way responsible.
However the petitioners with an oblique reasons foisted a false case in active collusion with the policy by creating a false crime records against this respondent driver.
Rest of the averments of the petition are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The respondent No.3/Reliance General Insurance Company Limited appeared and filed written statement admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 in favour of the respondent No.1 covering the alleged accident date, subject to the terms and conditions.
However negligence on the part of the driver of its insured car is denied.

Per contra it is alleged that the unfortunate accident occurred due to the rash & negligent act of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 came from Kanakapura side towards Malavalli side in opposite direction, driven on extreme its right side road and dashed to the car.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is submitted that the insured had knowingly entrusted his car to a driver who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said class of vehicle.
Further the car was plied in a public place without having valid permit and fitness certificate.
On account of conscious breach of terms & conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non -compliance of Sections 134(c) & 158(6) of IMV Act is pleaded.
Contending so prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MF-8055 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
Bhagyalakshmi

3) What order or award ?
7. The petitioner herself examined as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 12 were marked on her behalf.
Dr.Nagaraj.
B.N is examined as PW.2.
Ex . P.13
was marked through this witness.
The driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 was examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.3.

The Legal Claim Manager of the respondent No.3 was examined as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R1 & 2 documents.
8.
Heard both counsels for the petitioners and respondents on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1:
The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint, the jurisdictional police registered a FIR against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 and took up investigation.
During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them.
There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place.
The death of the deceased person due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident is also not in conflict.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

The question as to who was responsible for the accident has to be answered by looking into the evidence on record, perusal of which makes it evident that the Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 came and dashed against the front left side of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, as a result of which the petitioner sustained injuries and other inmates of the car succumbed on the spot.
11. PW.1 stated that stated that she was traveling as passenger in an offending vehicle KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA- 42-F-1745 from Kanakapura towards Halagur side.
The driver of the offending bus has driven with high speed and dashed against the Toyota car and after dragged the car at a distance of 50-75 feet from the accident spot.
The driver of the car was proceeding on correct side road and on proper lane from the opposite direction to an offending vehicle KSRTC bus.
During the course of her cross-examination, she admitted that she was sitting beside the driver seat on first seat.
She admitted that the road was busy road and the accident took place near the Kennare Gate.
She admitted that the bus which was proceeding at left side on the road, suddenly came towards right side and dashed to the car which was proceeding opposite to the bus on the left side.
She stated that if the bus driver had been drove the vehicle at his side, accident could have been avoided.
Nothing significant could be extracted from PW.2's mouth to disbelieve her presence at the spot of the accident, at the time of its occurrence.

4 12.
Further on perusal of complaint given by one Shivalingegowda he being complainant witness in charge sheet.

He stated that on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m, one green Coloured Qualis car was coming from Halagur side with high speed in a zig zag manner and at the same time one KSRTC bus which was coming from Kanakapura side with high speed in rash and negligent manner and both have coming with high speed and themselves have caused the accident on head on collision.
He is third person.
He cannot be suspected that he is telling lie.
The complaint lodged by Shivalingegowda clearly shows that there was gross negligence of drivers of both vehicles.
As per the contents there was more negligence of driver of Qualis car.
13. The other tortfeasor i.e., driver of the KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 (RW.1) who vehemently asserted that the said bus was express bus from Kanakapura to Halaguru.
He stated that the said road is NH-948 and the said road is straight road.
He further admitted that at the time of driving the vehicles were came opposite side could have been seen, he had seen the qualis car from 10 feet distance.
He further admitted that their was express bus, therefore there was a schedule to reach the destination.
The width of the road is 20 feet and accident took place at 4.30 p.m.

The learned counsel for petitioners put some questions to the driver of the KSRTC bus (RW.1) as :
"Question : Why you had taken the bus on right side on the road ?
Answer : The driver of the car came opposite side in zig zag manner, he came on left side of the road i.e on my side, so I had taken the bus on right side to avoid the accident".
RW.1 further admitted that the left front portion was damaged and has not produced photo of damaged bus.
He stated that he has not given any complaint as accident took place due to the negligence of the Qualis car, because he was also injured.

He stated that after 4 days from the date of accident he had taken bail from jurisdictional police and the criminal case is still pending at JMFC,
Kanakapura.
These elicitation make it amply clear that as RW.1 was driving his bus at a high speed and in a rash manner and bus dragged the car for certain distance.

A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to death due to the careless act of RW.1.
14.
From the testimonies of PW1 and complainant it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash & negligent driving of the both drivers.

Based on FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.7) against the drivers of KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01- MF-8055 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the drivers of both car & KSRTC bus.
If driver of car had driven his car in his side and in normal speed, the accident could have been avoided.
Accordingly if KSRTC bus driver was driving the bus in normal speed also it could have been avoided.
15. Thus the unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the drivers of the car and KSRTC bus.

A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the Bhagyalakshmi S vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196267738/
5 maximum, unfortunately has lead to injuries cased to the petitioner due to the careless act of drivers of both car and KSRTC bus.

The self serving statement of the driver of the KSRTC bus cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.

Be that as it may the inference that can be drawn from the police documents and evidence of PW.1 is that the driver of car and the driver of KSRTC bus were responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Thereby the negligence attributed towards driver of car and driver of KSRTC bus in the ratio of 70 :
30.

With this observation Issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16. ISSUE NO.2 : AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has exhibited her Aadhar card at Ex.P.11 wherein her date of birth is shown as 01.01.1993.
This indicates she was aged (30 years 7 months 27 days) 31 years on the date of accident.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in her evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 28.08.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
17. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Right patella fracture.
It is needless to say that the injuries are grievous in nature.
The discharge summary of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru (Ex.P.8) indicates that the petitioner was taken treatment as an inpatient from 31.08.2023 to 08.09.2023 (9 days).

During the course of treatment she undergone surgeries in the form of :
ORIF with TBW for right patella fracture done on 02.09.2023.
18.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries she has become disabled and has thereby lost her earning capacity.

Therefore she got examined Dr.Nagaraj. B.N as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has total physical disability of the right lower limb at 40% and whole body disability at 13%.

During the Bhagyalakshmi S vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196267738/
6 course of cross examination PW.2 admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He stated that the fracture was united without any deformity.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively,
as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor,
the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 7%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 7%.
19.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 9 days is proved with a help of discharge summaries.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.10,800/- (1,200 X 9) is awarded under this head.
20. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for atleast 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.48,000/- (16,000 X 3) under this head.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P10, the petitioner has spent Rs.8,982/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,982/- which is rounded off to Rs.9,000/- towards medical expenses.
23. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,15,040/- (Rs.16,000 X 12 X 16 X 7/100) which is rounded off to Rs.2,15,000/- is awarded under this head.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is Bhagyalakshmi S vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196267738/
7 awarded under this head.
25. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.60,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

26. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 10,800-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 48,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 9,000-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 2,15,000-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7

Future medical expenses :
40,000-00 Total 4,22,800-00 27.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
28. Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where injuries / death has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasors.

Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondents No.1 to 3 herein are jointly & severally liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondents No.1 & 3 being the insurers of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and car bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-MF-8055 and are primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 30 : 70, within one month from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,22,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondents No.1 & 3 are liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest in the ratio of 30 : 70, within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the drivers of both car & KSRTC bus.
If driver of car had driven his car in his side and in normal speed, the accident could have been avoided.
Accordingly if KSRTC bus driver was driving the bus in normal speed also it could have been avoided.
15. Thus the unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the drivers of the car and KSRTC bus.
A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the Bhagyalakshmi S vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196267738/
5 maximum, unfortunately has lead to injuries cased to the petitioner due to the careless act of drivers of both car and KSRTC bus.
The self serving statement of the driver of the KSRTC bus cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.
Be that as it may the inference that can be drawn from the police documents and evidence of PW.1 is that the driver of car and the driver of KSRTC bus were responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively,
as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor,
the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 7%, cannot be ruled out.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
28. Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where injuries / death has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasors.

Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondents No.1 to 3 herein are jointly & severally liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,22,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondents No.1 & 3 are liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest in the ratio of 30 : 70, within a period of one month from the date of award.
Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
